title: JSON-first plan engine (layout v3) with a Python API and generated Markdown views
decision:
1. A plan is a directory of JSON documents — `plan.json`, `brief.json`, `phases/<Pn>/phase.json`, `phases/<Pn>/<Pn.m>.json` (one file per item), `phases/<Pn>/<Pn.m>/<U#>.json` (work units), `decisions/<D#>.json` — plus append-only `log.jsonl`. Every document validates against a JSON Schema in `packages/task/schemas/plan/v1/` (Draft 2020-12, closed keyword profile). JSON is the only source of truth.
2. Agents and humans change a plan only through `packages/task/scripts/plan.py` / `task.plan` Python API. Each mutation validates, writes canonical JSON (schema key order, indent 2, UTF-8) atomically under a file lock, and regenerates the views.
3. Exactly six human views — `index.md`, `plan.md`, `roadmap.md`, `status.md`, `handoff.md`, `open-questions.md` — are rendered from JSON by templates with partials (own Mustache subset).
4. The item spec and its volatile `result` live in the same item file; history lives in `log.jsonl`. There are no generated state files, bundles, decision views or digest seals.
5. Item schema is the maximal union of the 16 v2 fields plus `related` (typed links incl. `P1.2` and qualified refs), `task_files` (hint, not a write limit), `artifacts` (relative paths), `decisions`, `rag {need,status}`, `review {mode,reviewer}`, `authority`, `units` (work units in the item workspace `phases/<Pn>/<Pn.m>/`, D3), `examples`.
6. The executor's input is a generated context pack (`context/<item>.md`) built from JSON at `start`, ordered Goal → Scope → Context → Decisions → Upstream → Reads → Files → Lessons → Done-when.
7. Log: lifecycle events are written by the API; agents write only sparse friction events (`deviation, blocker, difficulty, assumption, note`) with one command; the next context pack replays them.
8. Generated files (views, plan-local `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, `context/`, `_v2/`) are regenerated on every mutation and on out-of-band JSON edits (harness hooks, `check`/`render`), and every provider is told to ignore them through a global instruction, plan-local guard files and hooks (`research/00-design.md` §13; owner M2).
9. The layout is called `v3`; v2 is not readable by the new runtime (no legacy, D4).
rationale:
- Markdown carriers are parsed by regex and re-formatted differently by each provider; JSON + schema + API gives one canonical shape and machine checks (R2) — this is the owner's core pain (B1, B2).
- No existing tool provides schema-validated plans with generated views; Task Master's field set and beads' "one source of truth, views are exports" lesson are adopted (R1). Vendoring was rejected: `lib/task` stays stdlib-only and the needed schema/template subsets are small (R7).
- Keeping `result` inside the item file removes the v2 spec/state split whose digests caused `BATCH_STALE` and byte-fresh failures (`roadmap/2026-10-02-task-plan-run-rigidity.md`).
- Codex guidance favours short instructions and task context in Goal/Context/Constraints/Done-when form (R5): protocol logic moves into code; the context pack carries the task-specific context.
- Rejected: YAML (needs a parser outside stdlib); SQLite/Dolt (not diffable, not reviewable in PRs); one big `plan.json` (B4 wants per-item files); generated per-item state files (two owners of one fact).
consequences: Commands, canon and adapters are rewritten to the API (P3.1); the v2 runtime is deleted (P3.2, D2).
Consumers `harness` (review-gate, Stop hook) and `artifex` (slice compiler) move to `plan.py` (P3.1).
